title.en: States and neighbours of India (additional, not in the textbook)

text.en:
In class a huge map of India hung on the wall. Latha pointed at her state, Tamil Nadu, in the south.
"Which countries are next to us?" asked the teacher.
"Pakistan, Nepal, China, Bhutan, Bangladesh and Myanmar are on land," said Latha, "and Sri Lanka is across the sea."

India is divided into states and union territories. Each state has its own government and capital, and many have their own language. Delhi is the capital of India.
India has neighbours on land: Pakistan and Afghanistan in the north-west, China, Nepal and Bhutan in the north, and Bangladesh and Myanmar in the east.
Sri Lanka and the Maldives are island neighbours in the Indian Ocean. India has a long coastline. The Himalayas lie in the north and the Indian Ocean in the south.
India is divided into states and union territories. Delhi is the capital of India.
Pakistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh and Myanmar share a land border with India.
Sri Lanka and the Maldives are island neighbours in the Indian Ocean.
The Himalayas are in the north and the Indian Ocean is in the south.

problem.en: Which neighbour of India is an island country to the south?

text.en: The countries on land touch India's border.
Sri Lanka lies across the sea in the south.
So Sri Lanka is the island neighbour. The Maldives is another.

why.en: Both are in the Indian Ocean.

prompt.en: A friend says Sri Lanka shares a land border with India. How will you correct this?

requiredIdeas.en: Sri Lanka is an island separated from India by the sea.
Land neighbours include Nepal and Bangladesh.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking all neighbours share a land border.

points.en: India has states and union territories; Delhi is the capital.
Land neighbours include Pakistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh and Myanmar.
Sri Lanka and the Maldives are island neighbours.
